newsitem.title: USA: IBM to release Q4 after market close Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: IBM to release Q4 after market close Jan 21.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp will release its fourth quarter earnings after the stock market closes on Tuesday, January 21, a change for the computer giant which for years has released its earnings before the U.S. stock market opens, analysts said.

But analysts said they do not believe the change has any negative implications for the quarter and said that IBM is releasing earnings after the market's close to avoid the volatility in its stock that has occurred during its conference call with Wall Street analysts. IBM will also hold its meeting/conference call sometime after earnings are released.

"I don't think it's relative to their quarterly performance," said Gary Helmig, a SoundView Financial analyst. "What was happening is that they would release the numbers and they would have people in and out of the stock while the meeting was going on. They decided it made a lot more sense to do this when the market wasn't trading."
Helmig said he still is maintaining his estimates of $3.93 a share for the fourth quarter. "I'm not hearing anything bad (about the quarter)," Helmig said.
Many technology companies, especially those on the West Coast, release their earnings after the stock market closes.
An IBM spokesman said that IBM recently conducted an internal review of its entire earnings process, which included discussions with members of the investment community.

"Many members told us they would like us to release earnings after the close," said an IBM spokesman. "So it's a combination of internal review and comments from the investment community." He declined to comment about the volatility of IBM's stock on earnings days and whether this was a factor in IBM's decision.
"Many technology companies release their earnings after the close," the spokesman said.
IBM said the timing of earnings releases for future quarters will be decided after the company tries out the new procedure, and after it receives feedback from Wall Street analysts.
